Report experimental model, behavioral/electrophysiologic results, mechanistic evidence, and PMID or citation.'}

The primary research paper is **“The bradykinin B1 receptor antagonist BI113823 reverses inflammatory hyperalgesia by desensitization of peripheral and spinal neurons,”** *European Journal of Pain* (2015), **PMID: 25088373**.

In Wistar rats tested 24 hours after paw injection of complete Freund’s adjuvant (CFA), BI113823 reduced CFA-induced mechanical hyperalgesia after both oral and intrathecal administration. Electrophysiologically, it reduced mechanosensitivity in peripheral saphenous-nerve afferents and spinal nociceptive-specific neurons, but not spinal wide-dynamic-range neurons. B1-receptor gene expression was increased in peripheral and spinal neural tissue. Together, these results support effects at both peripheral and spinal levels. The evidence for “desensitization” is functional—reduced neuronal mechanosensitivity; the abstract does not report a direct molecular receptor-desensitization assay.

The evidence supports **yes**. In a CFA-induced inflammatory hyperalgesia rat model, BI113823 reduced mechanical hyperalgesia after both oral and intrathecal administration. Electrophysiology showed reduced mechanosensitivity in peripheral saphenous-nerve afferents and spinal nociceptive-specific neurons, but not spinal wide-dynamic-range neurons.
